Script checksum, syntax, lock availability, ledger data, OS release, and kernel were verified after recovery.

#!/bin/sh
set -eu

base=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")/.." && pwd)
lock="$base/.reconcile.lock"

# Keep this descriptor open for the life of the process.  The kernel releases
# the lock automatically on normal exit, error, or interruption.
exec 9>"$lock"
if ! flock -n 9; then
  printf '%s\n' 'reconcile: another invocation already owns the job' >&2
  exit 75
fi

while IFS= read -r batch; do
  [ -n "$batch" ] || continue
  if ! grep -Fqx -- "$batch" "$base/ledger.tsv"; then
    sleep 1
    printf '%s\n' "$batch" >> "$base/ledger.tsv"
  fi
done < "$base/pending.tsv"
ANTRIEB_EOF
chmod 755 bin/reconcile
sh -n bin/reconcile && sed -n '1,240p' bin/reconcile && stat -c '%a %U %G %n' bin/reconcile
